items.title: India's Energy Scenario & Mix
items.body:
## Demand & import dependence

- India is the **world's third-largest energy consumer**; demand is rising fast with growth and urbanisation, though **per-capita consumption stays well below the global average**.
- **Import dependence is a core energy-security worry** — India imports about **85-88% of its crude oil** and a large share of its natural gas (LNG), plus some coal.

## The generation mix

- **Coal remains the single largest source of electricity generation** (~70%+ of generation) even though its share of *installed capacity* is falling.
- The transition strategy: rapidly add **non-fossil capacity** (solar, wind, hydro, nuclear) while coal generation is phased *down* (not abruptly out) to protect base-load supply.
- Drivers of transition — climate commitments (net-zero 2070), energy security (cutting imports), falling renewable costs, and air-pollution concerns.
keyPoints: India is the world's 3rd-largest energy consumer; per-capita consumption is below the global average.
Crude oil import dependence is about 85-88 percent; India also imports LNG.
Coal is still the largest source of electricity generation (~70%+ of generation).
Non-fossil capacity is being added rapidly while coal is phased down, not banned.
Transition drivers: net-zero 2070, energy security, falling RE costs, air pollution.
items.source: PIB / MNRE / Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (pib.gov.in)

items.title: Renewable Targets, Capacity Milestones & Solar/Wind
items.body:
## The 500 GW goal and milestones

- At **COP26 (Glasgow, 2021)** India pledged **500 GW of non-fossil installed capacity by 2030** (a Panchamrit commitment).
- **India crossed 50% of installed capacity from non-fossil sources in 2025** — about five years *ahead* of its NDC target — and its **total installed capacity crossed ~500 GW** around 2025.
- The earlier **175 GW (by 2022)** renewable target has been superseded by the 500 GW non-fossil goal.

## Solar programmes

- **National Solar Mission (2010)** and large **solar parks** (Bhadla in Rajasthan, Pavagada in Karnataka) anchor utility-scale solar.
- **PM-KUSUM** solarises **agriculture** — standalone solar pumps and grid-connected solar for farmers.
- **PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (Feb 2024)** — **rooftop solar** for **1 crore households**, up to **300 free units/month**, outlay **Rs 75,021 crore**.

## Wind

- **Gujarat and Tamil Nadu** lead in installed wind capacity; India is developing **offshore wind** (viability-gap funding off Gujarat/Tamil Nadu).

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Non-fossil target | 500 GW by 2030 |
| 50% non-fossil capacity | Achieved 2025 (ahead of NDC) |
| PM Surya Ghar | 1 crore homes, 300 free units, Rs 75,021 cr |
keyPoints: 500 GW non-fossil by 2030 target announced at COP26 (Panchamrit).
India reached 50% non-fossil installed capacity in 2025, ahead of its NDC.
Total installed capacity crossed about 500 GW around 2025.
PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (Feb 2024): rooftop solar, 1 crore homes, up to 300 free units, Rs 75,021 cr.
PM-KUSUM solarises agriculture; National Solar Mission and solar parks (Bhadla, Pavagada) anchor solar.
Gujarat and Tamil Nadu lead wind capacity; offshore wind is being developed.

items.title: National Green Hydrogen Mission
items.body:
## What it is

- **Green hydrogen** is produced by **electrolysis of water using renewable electricity** — zero-carbon, unlike **grey** (from natural gas) or **blue** (gas + carbon capture) hydrogen.
- The **National Green Hydrogen Mission** was approved in **January 2023** with an initial outlay of **Rs 19,744 crore**.

## Targets & components

- Target: about **5 MMT (million tonnes) of green hydrogen per year by 2030**, supported by roughly **125 GW** of added renewable capacity.
- **SIGHT** (Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition) gives incentives for **electrolyser manufacturing** and **green-hydrogen production**.
- Aims to cut fossil-fuel imports, decarbonise fertiliser/refining/steel, and make India a **green-hydrogen export hub**.
- **Andhra Pradesh** has announced a green-hydrogen thrust in its clean-energy policy, leveraging its coastline and renewables.
keyPoints: Green hydrogen = electrolysis of water using renewable power (zero carbon).
National Green Hydrogen Mission approved Jan 2023, outlay Rs 19,744 crore.
Target ~5 MMT green hydrogen per year by 2030, ~125 GW added RE capacity.
SIGHT scheme incentivises electrolyser manufacturing and hydrogen production.
Aims to decarbonise fertiliser, refining and steel, and build an export hub.

items.title: Nuclear Energy — Three-Stage Programme, SMRs & Reforms
items.body:
## Three-stage programme (Homi Bhabha)

- **Stage 1 — PHWRs** fuelled by **natural uranium**, producing plutonium-239.
- **Stage 2 — Fast Breeder Reactors (FBRs)** using Pu-239 + U-238; they *breed* more fuel and begin the **thorium-uranium-233** cycle. The **Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR)** at **Kalpakkam** (run by **BHAVINI**) began **core fuel loading in 2024** — a key Stage-2 milestone.
- **Stage 3 — thorium-based breeders** exploiting India's **vast thorium reserves** (monazite in coastal beach sands of Kerala, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh).

## Institutions & plants

- Under the **Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)**: **BARC** (research, Trombay), **IGCAR** (fast-reactor R&D, Kalpakkam), **NPCIL** (operates commercial plants), **BHAVINI** (fast breeder). **Kudankulam** (Tamil Nadu) hosts Russian VVER reactors.

## Recent policy (2025-26)

- **Nuclear Energy Mission** (Union Budget 2025-26): **Rs 20,000 crore** for **Small Modular Reactor (SMR)** R&D, at least **five indigenous SMRs by 2033**, and **100 GW nuclear by 2047** (from ~8-9 GW today).
- **SHANTI Act (2026)**: landmark law **opening the nuclear power sector to private participation**, overhauling the legacy Atomic Energy Act 1962 framework and related civil-nuclear-liability provisions (linked to the 123 Agreement) to attract investment.
keyPoints: Three-stage programme: PHWR (natural U) to FBR (breeds Pu, starts Th cycle) to thorium breeders.
PFBR at Kalpakkam (BHAVINI) began core fuel loading in 2024 — Stage-2 milestone.
DAE bodies: BARC (research), IGCAR (fast-reactor R&D), NPCIL (power plants), BHAVINI (FBR); Kudankulam has VVER reactors.
Nuclear Energy Mission (Budget 2025-26): Rs 20,000 cr for SMRs, 5 indigenous SMRs by 2033, 100 GW nuclear by 2047.
SHANTI Act (2026) opens nuclear power to private participation, reforming the Atomic Energy Act 1962 framework.
India has large thorium but limited uranium, driving the thorium-based Stage 3.
items.mnemonic: Three-stage fuel ladder 'U-Pu-Th' = natural Uranium to Plutonium breeding to Thorium.

items.title: Bioenergy, Energy Efficiency, EVs & Net-Zero
items.body:
## Bioenergy

- **Ethanol Blending Programme** — India reached about **20% ethanol blending (E20)** around **2025**, cutting oil imports and emissions; ethanol comes from **sugarcane, molasses, surplus grain and crop residue**.
- **SATAT** promotes **Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG)** from agricultural/urban waste; **waste-to-energy** plants add to the mix.

## Energy efficiency

- **BEE** (Bureau of Energy Efficiency), under the **Energy Conservation Act 2001**, coordinates efficiency.
- **PAT** ('Perform, Achieve and Trade') is a market mechanism for energy-intensive industries issuing tradable **ESCerts**.
- **Standards & Labelling (star ratings)** on appliances and **UJALA** (efficient LED distribution) cut household demand.

## EVs & storage

- **PM E-DRIVE (2024)** succeeds the **FAME** schemes to push EV adoption and charging infrastructure.
- **Battery storage (BESS)** and **pumped-storage hydro** firm up variable solar/wind.

## Net-zero & global role

- **Net-zero by 2070** (Panchamrit, COP26); India co-founded the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** — launched with **France at CoP21 (Paris, 2015)**, **headquartered at Gurugram (Gurgaon), India** — and leads **Mission LiFE**.
keyPoints: India reached ~20% ethanol blending (E20) around 2025; ethanol from sugarcane/molasses/grain, not petroleum.
SATAT promotes Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG) from waste and biomass.
BEE (Energy Conservation Act 2001) runs PAT (ESCerts), star labelling and UJALA (LEDs).
PM E-DRIVE (2024) succeeds FAME to boost EVs and charging infrastructure.
Net-zero by 2070 (Panchamrit); India leads the International Solar Alliance (co-founded with France, CoP21 2015, HQ Gurugram) and Mission LiFE.

items.title: Andhra Pradesh — Energy & Pumped Storage
items.body:
## AP's clean-energy push

- Andhra Pradesh has a strong **solar and wind** resource base and one of India's **largest identified potentials for pumped-storage hydro projects (PSPs)** — exploiting its terrain and reservoirs.
- The state's **clean-energy policy** promotes **renewables, green hydrogen and energy storage**, aiming to attract large investments and position AP as a green-energy and storage hub.

## Pumped storage — the 'water battery'

- A **pumped-storage plant** stores energy by **pumping water to an upper reservoir when surplus (cheap) power is available** and **generating electricity by releasing it during peak demand** — vital for balancing variable solar and wind.
- The **Pinnapuram Integrated Renewable Energy Storage Project (Kurnool district)** combines **solar + wind + a very large pumped-storage** component and is among the world's largest such integrated projects.

## Conventional & significance

- AP also has substantial **thermal** capacity and hosts coastal sites suited to renewables and green-hydrogen; the state has projected periods of **power surplus**.
keyPoints: Andhra Pradesh has one of India's largest identified pumped-storage-hydro potentials.
AP's clean-energy policy promotes renewables, green hydrogen and energy storage.
Pumped storage pumps water uphill on surplus power and generates at peak demand (a 'water battery').
Pinnapuram (Kurnool) integrates solar, wind and a very large pumped-storage unit.
AP also has thermal capacity and coastal sites suited to renewables and green hydrogen.

items.title: Andhra Pradesh — Renewable Energy Snapshot (2026)
items.body:
## Capacity commissioned (~2026)

- AP has commissioned about **14,833 MW** of renewables (NREDCAP, Aug 2026).

| Source | ~MW |
|---|---|
| Ground solar | 7,049 |
| Wind | 4,461 |
| Pumped storage | 1,680 |
| Rooftop solar | 1,015 |
| **Total RE** | **~14,833** |

## Targets & flagship projects

- Roadmap target: **~160 GW green energy by 2047**; pipeline ~25.58 GW solar, ~5.78 GW wind, ~18.95 GW pumped storage.
- **Pinnapuram** (Kurnool): integrated renewables + very large pumped storage.
- **Pudimadaka** (Anakapalli, near Visakhapatnam): NTPC Green hydrogen hub — among India's largest (~1,200 TPD).
- **Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park** (1,000 MW). AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024.
keyPoints: AP has commissioned ~14,833 MW of renewables (NREDCAP, 2026), solar-led.
Long-term target: ~160 GW green energy by 2047 with a large pumped-storage pipeline.
Pinnapuram (Kurnool) integrates renewables with very large pumped storage.
Pudimadaka (Anakapalli) NTPC Green hydrogen hub is among India's largest (~1,200 TPD).
Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park = 1,000 MW; AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024.
